key_concepts: Motion is a change in position over a time interval
Distance is the total length of the entire path travelled
Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance between initial and final positions
Displacement depends only on starting and ending points, not the path taken
The SI unit for both distance and displacement is the meter
Distance can be equal to displacement when motion is in a straight line without changing d
Displacement can never be greater than distance
In one-dimensional motion, opposite directions are subtracted to find displacement
Total distance is found by adding all path segments regardless of direction
A straight-line shortcut between two places represents displacement
Actual travel routes between two places represent distance
